CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Labuhanbatu Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Labuhanbatu.
4. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, restriction or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
5. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a Child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a person of female gender.
8. Violence against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of Women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against Children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of Children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a Woman and Child who experiences violence and/or threat of violence.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecution, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that Violence against Women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from acts of Violence and discrimination.
13. Service is actions taken as soon as possible to Victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that Violence against Victims will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying Victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of Violence Victims.
15. Gender is the difference in characteristics, roles, functions and status between Women and men which is not based on biological differences, but rather based on socio-cultural relations influenced by the broader structure of society.
16. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate Gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
17. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as Dinas PPPA, is the office that administers the affairs of Women's empowerment and Child Protection.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated Service center in efforts to empower Women and Children established by the Regional Government with active community participation which includes an information center, consultation center, complaint service, initial health care, counseling, legal assistance, repatriation and social reintegration, shelter/temporary safe house, as well as a referral center.
19. Safe House is a shelter/temporary protection house for Victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of Victims from threats and danger from perpetrators, and is only known to interested parties such as certain personnel at UPT P2TP2A for reasons of Victim safety and security.
20. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter abbreviated as SOP, is standard steps that must be taken in protecting Victims starting from complaint/identification, rehabilitation, health, Social Rehabilitation, advocacy up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or Victims.
21. Family is the smallest unit in Society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and Child, or mother and Child or Family by blood in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree and/or if any up to the fourth degree.
22. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have Family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, representation, and/or Household workers and reside in that Household.
23. Society is individuals, Families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of South Labuhanbatu Regency.
25. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out their social functions properly in the life of Society.

Article 15
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:
a. implement policies for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence established by the government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various NGOs concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(3) In order to carry out the obligations as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, the Regional Government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children in 1 (one) Regional Action Plan as a basis for regional apparatus in implementing protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
(4) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3) constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD).
(5) The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (3) is further regulated by a Regulation of the Regent.

Article 17
The obligations of the Family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letters c and d have full responsibility to prevent all forms of Violence and protect Women and Children as members of the Family.

Article 37
(1) Social behavioral change is carried out with the aim of changing the way of thinking, having attitudes, and acting in accordance with parenting and education patterns that protect Children.
(2) Behavioral change is intended to change policies, programs and budget allocations along with their action plans to change the social behavior of individuals, groups, government and non-government institutions to implement Child protection.
(3) Regional Apparatus authorized to implement behavioral change as regulated in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are Regional Apparatus in charge of social affairs, religion, health, education, Community empowerment, population, manpower, information and communication as well as Child protection under the coordination of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of the protection of Women and Children.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "the principle of respect for human rights" is that the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence is to guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of victims of violence as a manifestation of respect for human rights.
Letter b What is meant by "the right to life, survival, and development" is the rights as regulated in the provisions of the 1945 Constitution.
Letter c What is meant by "Non-discriminatory" is the attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions on the basis of age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion, and inter-group classification.
Letter d What is meant by the principle of the best interests of the Child is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the child must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by "the principle of Gender equality and justice" is a process of equality and conditions for men and Women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Letter f What is meant by "the principle of protection of the Rights of victims" is the protection of the personal self, Family, honor, dignity, and property under their control, a sense of security and protection from threats of fear, freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Article 35
(1) The Regional Government may establish a Gender Mainstreaming Working Group.
(2) The Working Group as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of members from regional apparatus and relevant vertical institutions/agencies as well as non-governmental institutions, higher education institutions, the business sector, and religious-based institutions, as well as the community, that work for the protection of Women and Children.
(3) The establishment of the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be stipulated by a Regent Decision.
(4) Each member of the Working Group as referred to in paragraph (2) may appoint a Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point.

Article 34
paragraph (1) What is meant by “Gender Responsive Budget Planning” is budget planning that accommodates equity for women and men in obtaining access, benefits, participation, decision-making, control over resources, as well as equality in opportunities and chances to enjoy the results of development.
paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.

Article 34
(1) Every regional apparatus is obligated to conduct gender-responsive budgeting planning.
(2) Gender-responsive budgeting planning as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be coordinated by the regional apparatus in the field of Women and Children.

Article 43
(1) Community social institutions as referred to in Article 42 paragraph (2) letter d, implementing the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence must coordinate with P2TP2A.
(2) The Regional Government encourages the business sector to participate in the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
(3) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. socialization to employees within the company environment regarding the dangers of acts of Violence against Women and Children; and
b. assistance as a form of corporate social responsibility.

Article 28
(1) Data and information as referred to in Article 27 shall become material for the formulation of policies, programs, budgets, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
(2) The formulation of policies, programs, budgets, monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented with the following mechanisms: a. creating mapping, long-term, medium-term and short-term plans; b. creating agreements on the periodization of monthly and annual working meetings; c. creating agreements on the collection, mapping and presentation of data among regional apparatus organizations;
d. incorporating agreements into programs and budgets; and e. conducting scheduling of monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY AND BUSINESS PARTICIPATION
Article 42
(1) Every person may participate in providing protection to Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by: a. reporting acts of Violence against Women and/or Children; b. providing first aid to Victims;
c. independently disseminating the rights of Women and Children; and/or d. establishing independent community social institutions.

Article 29
(1) Regional Apparatus with authority over Women and Children shall be obliged to prepare the formulation of service policy regarding the protection of Women and Children from acts of Violence.
(2) The formulation of service policy as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented through the following mechanism:
a. formulating case reporting policy related to Women and Children who become Victims of acts of Violence;
b. preparing reporting and referral mechanisms between regional apparatus organizations with authority over the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence with relevant agencies and with P2TP2A; and
c. preparing budget for the implementation of policy on the protection of Women and Children against acts of Violence.

Article 31
(1) The fulfillment of social welfare for Women and Children aims to prevent, reduce vulnerability risks and handle Victims of acts of Violence.
(2) The fulfillment of social welfare for Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Regional apparatus that oversees social issues.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 44
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out periodically by Regional Apparatus that has the authority for the empowerment of Women and Children against acts of Violence.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(4) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

4.2.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation clearly mandates education/awareness activities that include gender-related content. For example, Pasal 21 requires prevention through “kegiatan sosialisasi peraturan perundang-undangan… berkaitan dengan perlindungan hak Perempuan dan Anak” and “pemberdayaan dan penyadaran… dengan memberikan informasi, bimbingan dan/atau penyuluhan,” plus improving education access. Separately, Pasal 36 ayat (1) huruf d explicitly assigns the Gender Mainstreaming Working Group to conduct “sosialisasi, advokasi, koordinasi, dan pelatihan Pengarusutamaan Gender.” These provisions match the indicator’s idea of gender equality education/awareness (socialization/training on gender mainstreaming and women’s rights). The retrieved English candidates accurately reflect these Indonesian clauses, and the judge’s reasoning aligns with them. Therefore the ‘No’ golden label appears incorrect; the policy does include gender-equality-related education/awareness measures.
